proof.odd_CH: For traceless Hermitian3 B with eigenvalues b1+b2+b3=0, sum b_i^4=(sum b_i^2)^2/2 by expanding b3=-b1-b2. Polarizing this polynomial gives 4Tr(X^2Y^2)+2Tr(XYXY)=Tr(X^2)Tr(Y^2)+2(Tr XY)^2.
proof.odd_collection: For arbitrary traceless Hermitian3 X_a, let R_ab=Tr X_a X_b and S=sum_a X_a^2. Summed polarization gives sum_ab Tr({X_a,X_b}^2)=(Tr S)^2+2||R||F^2-2Tr S^2. HS triangle and odd_CH give ||S||HS<=sum_a ||X_a^2||HS=Tr S/sqrt(2). Consequently the anticommutator sum is >=2||R||F^2. Equivalently sum_ab ||{X_a,X_b}-(2/3)R_ab I3||HS^2 >=(2/3)||R||F^2. This is a quantitative trace/parity residual, not a representation-name exclusion.
proof.traceful_projection: If s!=0 let P project onto s-perp in real field-index R4, rank3; if s=0 choose any rank3 P. Rotate field indices orthogonally so P selects three coordinates. Their A combinations are traceless because Tr A=-s. The sum of squared traceless anticommutators over those three directions is a subset of the full orthogonally invariant nonnegative sum. Thus full residual >=(2/3)||PTP||F^2. Scalars and the fourth arbitrary Hermitian3 field were NOT discarded.
proof.quartic: The exact flat quartic is qJ=256 sum_mu,nu Tr({Phi_mu,Phi_nu}^2). Trace decomposition on the3 block plus the scalar gives qJ=(1024/3)||T||F^2+1024||ss^T||F^2+256||F3||F^2, F3_mu,nu={A_mu,A_nu}-(2/3)T_mu,nu I3. Hence qJ>=(1024/3)[||T||F^2+(1/2)||PTP||F^2]+1024|s|^4.
proof.first_route: The scalar-block rank-one residual alone gives qJ>=4096[||G||F^2+(1/3)||G-ss^T||F^2]. Optimizing its rank-one residual yields qJ>=4096[g1^2+(4/3)sum_i>1 gi^2]. The resulting global-moment bound is weaker than the incoming floor. It is retained as a failed route; the odd_CH collection inequality is a materially different traceful3-block route.
proof.alternative_global: Combining the first-route exact decomposition with odd_collection adds (8192/3)||PGP||F^2. Rank-one approximation/interlacing give ||G-ss^T||F^2>=sum_i>1 gi^2 and ||PGP||F^2>=sum_i>1 gi^2, so qJ>=4096[g1^2+2sum_i>1 gi^2]. Weighted Cauchy yields the independent global-moment lower bound reported below.
proof.dual_pressure: For Q_P(T)=||T||F^2+(1/2)||PTP||F^2, the positive operator T->PTP is an orthogonal projection on the real symmetric matrix space. Inverting I+(1/2)projection gives C-dual norm squared D(P)=||C||F^2-(1/3)||PCP||F^2. Weighted Cauchy proves (Tr CT)^2<=D(P) Q_P(T). Eigenvalue interlacing for compression to any3-plane gives ||PCP||F^2>=sum of the smallest3 eigenvalues(C)^2; hence D(P)<=D31=cmax^2+(2/3)sum_remaining c_i^2. This is uniform in s orientation and rank drops.
proof.all_angles: Native Fourier coefficients x_b(k) satisfy mean64 xx^T=C independently in EACH block for every continuous theta: all four samples per axis have zero sin/cos and sincos averages and sin^2=cos^2=1/2. Determinant is theta1=-3theta3 mod2pi; the3+1 character torus is connected. No angle minimizer, grid or centrality assumption is used.
